The proposed stealth Vivaldi antenna operates over 2 to 12 GHz ultrawide band.
Maximum radar cross section (RCS) reduction achieved is 14 dBsm.
The antenna uses a Taconic TLY-5 substrate with dielectric constant 2.2 and thickness 0.5 mm.
The antenna patch edges are modified using three pairs of arcs: quarter circle, half ellipse, and quarter circle plus rectangle.
Simulations were performed using HFSS based on the finite element method.
The antenna gain difference compared to the reference antenna is less than 1 dB in most bands.
The antenna maintains good voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) and radiation patterns similar to the reference antenna.
Monostatic radar cross section (MRCS) is reduced for both h-polarized and u-polarized incident waves.
Current distribution differs significantly between radiation and scattering modes, enabling targeted shaping for RCS reduction.
The antenna size reduction contributes to decreased high-frequency scattering.
Antennas 2 and 3 with partial modifications show less RCS reduction compared to the fully proposed antenna.
Measured and simulated radiation patterns at 7 GHz and 11 GHz show good agreement.
The feed line narrow end width is 0.4 mm, and the slot line starts from a circular slot stub with radius 19 mm.
The antenna is designed for military applications requiring low detectability.
The study was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China and Doctoral Program of Higher Education.
The proposed antenna achieves excellent radiation and stealth performance simultaneously.
The antenna is printed on a substrate sized 100 mm by 107 mm.
The shaping method is effective for antenna RCS reduction without compromising radiation performance.
The induced current amplitude and distribution are altered by the patch modifications, reducing scattering.
The antenna design considers multiple incident angles and polarizations for comprehensive RCS reduction.
